clue.text: Material used originally to wrap up a case with charge

definitions.text: Material used originally to wrap up a case with charge

parts.words: Material used originally to wrap up a case with charge
parts.note: a heavy paper whose name records its first use: rolling the casing that held a gun's powder charge

explanation.surface: An instruction for packing ammunition: what was first used to wrap a shell case?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a description: the stiff drawing paper artists use was first made for wrapping the powder and shot of a gun cartridge, so the clue's case with charge and its wrapping name the answer's two words.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick drawing stock takes its name from its early use in making the casings for firearm ammunition.

clue.text: Broadcast serials providing nothing for inspiration

indicators.note: broadcast as scattered, like seed thrown widely, so the letters of serials are rearranged

explanation.surface: Radio serials offer nothing to inspire the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like it belongs with radio serials, but it is the anagram signal. 'Inspiration' is breathing in, not creative spark.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room without ventilation has nothing to breathe in, and inspiration literally means drawing breath.

clue.text: Timothy and I abandoning one musician for another

indicators.note: abandoning says the letter I walks out of the musician's name

parts.note: a pianist is one kind of musician
taken as written

explanation.surface: Timothy and the speaker leave one musician to go off with another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes I out of PIANIST to leave PANIST, which follows TIM. The definition is 'another' musician: a pianist swapped for a player of a different instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum player is a second kind of orchestral performer, the other player the clue swaps in.

clue.text: Tipping a little Muscadet in ginger-beer, gets lit

indicators.note: Tipping says the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pouring a drop of white wine into ginger beer gets someone drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' marks DETINGI inside 'Muscadet in ginger-beer', and 'Tipping' turns it up the down grid. 'gets lit' suggests getting drunk but means catching fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ignited has been set on fire, and lit is the past tense for being set alight.

clue.text: Single odd clue I contrived about old fruit

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round another piece
contrived means artificially put together, so the letters of the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter admits writing one strange clue about an old fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges SINGLE ODD CLUE I, and 'about' puts that round O for 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a widely grown variety of eating apple with yellow-green skin.

clue.text: Not covering all the low digits

definitions.text: Not covering all the low digits

parts.words: Not covering all the low digits
parts.note: low digits are toes, the fingers at the bottom of the body; the shoe leaves some of them showing

explanation.surface: A remark about a shoe that leaves part of the foot bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low digits' sounds like small numbers but means toes, and the shoe described has an opening at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe with a small opening at the front lets the toes show through.

clue.text: Steer to just avoid being sunk going North

indicators.note: going North in a down clue means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: taken as written
in golf or snooker a ball lips when it catches the rim of the hole or pocket and stays out

explanation.surface: Advice to steer a boat so that it narrowly avoids sinking while heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going North' turns TO plus LIP upwards to read PILOT. To lip is a sporting term: the ball hits the edge of the hole or pocket and fails to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer a vessel or aircraft is to guide its course, the job of a navigator.

clue.text: Permanent marks on trousers

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
cords are corduroy trousers

explanation.surface: Lasting stains on someone's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Latin-based shorthand for 'about' or 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Written accounts kept to preserve facts are lasting documentation, entries that stay.

clue.text: Serious lack of care? I'm calling centre for repairs

indicators.note: things sent for repairs are taken apart and put back together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone phoning a service centre to report serious neglect of something broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repairs' makes an anagram of the fifteen letters of I'M CALLING CENTRE. The question mark marks the definition as a loose description of the legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave failure in a duty of care, serious enough to be an offence in law, is the legal term for this.

clue.text: Leave damaged tents in more spacious retail outlet

parts.note: to leave is to depart

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: damaged tents are knocked out of shape, so the word tents is rearranged

explanation.surface: Campers abandon their ruined tents for the roomier comfort of a big shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges TENTS into ENTST, and 'in' puts that inside MORE, giving MENTSTORE after DEPART.
explanation.definitionFit: A large shop with separate sections selling many kinds of goods under one roof is this kind of store.

clue.text: Wine that sparkles as it is knocked back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but here the word it is turned to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fizzy wine gets drunk quickly, just as it comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' sounds like drinking the wine but turns IT into TI, which follows AS; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian sparkling white comes from the Piedmont town of the same name.

clue.text: Indication of insight hard to find in articles

indicators.note: in says one letter goes inside the pair of articles

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, and two of them give A and A
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sign of understanding is hard to find in written pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' are the grammatical kind, here A and A, not pieces of writing; 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation shows sudden understanding, the moment the penny drops.

clue.text: Kind of automobile in Kansas City

definitions.meaning: a Wild West town in Kansas, known with City after its name

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a US car make and the frontier town in Kansas famous for Wyatt Earp.

clue.text: Record in athletic event US lost

indicators.note: lost says the letters of US go missing from the event's name

parts.note: the discus is a field event in athletics
taken as written

explanation.surface: An athletics meeting where the Americans lost a record-breaking event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes US off the end of DISCUS. 'Record' looks like a sporting best but is a gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record is a flat round platter, so the word for that shape names it.

clue.text: Present combination of lines and circle as artist

parts.note: to present is to donate
L stands for line, so two lines give LL
the letter O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A gift made of lines and a circle is offered up as an artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination of' and 'as' are links. The artist is the Florentine sculptor of the early Renaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century Florentine sculptor of the bronze David is one of the great Renaissance artists.

clue.text: Find fault with lack of parking for this?

definitions.text: Find fault with lack of parking for this?

indicators.note: with lack of says a letter is removed from the word before

parts.note: to carp is to find fault or complain
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A motorist grumbles about there being nowhere to leave a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P for 'parking' off CARP. Read as a whole, the clue is what a driver does when there is no parking for the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor vehicle is what needs parking, so a driver short of spaces grumbles on its behalf.

clue.text: Neighbour taking large piece of brass back

indicators.note: back says the instrument's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the tuba is the largest instrument in the brass section

explanation.surface: A neighbour borrows a big brass instrument and brings it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TUBA round. 'Neighbour' is a verb here: to border on something.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something as a verb is to border it or lie against it.

clue.text: Hotel worker taking beautiful woman, we hear, to dance

indicators.note: we hear says a word is said aloud and spelt as another

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A hotel employee takes a lovely woman out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes BELLE sound like BELL; 'taking' and 'to' are links. The hotel worker is an American porter who carries luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniformed porter who carries guests' luggage to their rooms, a US term.

clue.text: Spiritual leader of state? Not half!

indicators.note: only half of the state's ten-letter name is kept, its first five letters

parts.note: California is a US state

explanation.surface: Asked whether a state has a spiritual leader, someone replies with an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it means take half of CALIFORNIA. The spiritual leader is a variant spelling of the Muslim title also written caliph.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the religious and civil head of the Muslim world, successor to the Prophet; this is an alternative spelling.

clue.text: Kit order: "White robe for baptism"

parts.note: Kit is a pet name for Christopher, as is Chris
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An instruction from a supplier's catalogue: send one white christening gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit order' looks like a purchase of gear, but Kit is a name and the order an honour. The OM, Order of Merit, is a British distinction in the monarch's personal gift.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word names the white cloth or gown put on a child at christening as a sign of innocence.

clue.text: Jumble sale to flutter around in deceptive fashion

indicators.note: around says one word goes round the other

parts.note: to flutter is to fly, flapping wings

indicators.note: a jumble mixes things up, so the letters of sale are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jumble sale has people fluttering around it in a deceitful way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble' rearranges SALE into ALSE, and 'around' puts FLY round it. A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting untruthfully or insincerely is behaving dishonestly, the opposite of genuinely.

clue.text: Close in on earldom

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words on earldom

explanation.surface: Someone is closing in on inheriting an earldom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters inside 'on earldom'. 'Close' is the adjective meaning nearby, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close is nearby, only a short distance off.

clue.text: Radar, say, locating friend in the morning

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: AM stands for the morning, before noon
a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: Radar locates a friend early one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radar, say' looks like a detection device but is an example: radar comes from 'radio detection and ranging'. 'locating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is a word formed from the initials of radio detection and ranging, an example of an abbreviation pronounced as a word.

clue.text: Shocking weather conditions?

parts.note: shocking reads as terrible but also as giving electric shocks, the lightning of a thunderstorm

explanation.surface: Someone complains about dreadful weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like a complaint about the weather, but read literally it means full of electricity: a storm with thunder and lightning.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm with lightning flashes and thunder is a weather event charged with electricity.

clue.text: A pain in the neck one's endlessly upset about

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about another person who is a real pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CRICK to CRIC; with A in front, 'upset' turns ACRIC into the answer. 'one's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word means approximately and is used before dates, as in c. 1500.

clue.text: You cannot possibly know your secret is safe!

definitions.meaning: a promise not to tell anyone

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means it is impossible to say what will happen, and taken literally it promises that nobody will be told.

clue.text: Map my life story out in film

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A director plans to lay out their own life story as a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the fourteen letters of MAP MY LIFE STORY. The answer is Clint Eastwood's 1971 thriller about a radio DJ stalked by a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Clint Eastwood's 1971 debut as director, a psychological thriller.
